turns.text: /navigator INVESTIGATE Why does `timer backup --every 90` wait an hour and a half between runs instead of 90 seconds?

Short answer: a bare number is read as minutes, so `--every 90` means 90 minutes (5,400 seconds). How it happens: `main` in src/timer/cli.py:15 passes the `--every` value to `parse_duration`. In src/timer/durations.py, line 12 checks whether the last character is a unit (`s`, `m`, or `h`). `90` has none, so line 15 falls back to `DEFAULT_UNIT`, which line 4 sets to `m`, and line 16 returns 90 * 60 = 5400. This looks intended rather than accidental: README.md:9-10 documents that a number without a unit is minutes, and tests/test_durations.py:10-11 checks that `parse_duration('90')` returns 5400. I found no recorded reason for choosing minutes over seconds as the default; it has been there since the commit that added the parser. If you want 90 seconds, write `--every 90s`. This comes from reading the source, README, and tests; I did not run anything. You can ask `/navigator help` any time to see the other modes.
